note: Adapted from Haviland's original English description of 1898 (published as Termes dentatus, later placed in Amitermes); it describes the alates (male and female) and the soldier, and in the original the species is the type of the 'dentatus group'. The soldier description is cut off at the page by a plate caption, so this entry ends at the part read and nothing has been supplied.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The original published it as Termes dentatus and made it the type of the 'dentatus group'. The soldier has a body length of about 4.5 mm, an oval head and 14-segmented antennae; the alate has a wing length of 8—9 mm, the media lying closer to the submedia than to the subcosta and extending to the wing apex.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Male: body length 5—6 mm; head oval; antennae 15-segmented, segment 2 longer than segment 4, segment 3 variable in length; the epistoma more or less convex, prominent; anterior margin of the pronotum nearly straight, the anterolateral corners slightly inclined downwards; wing length 8—9 mm, the media closer to the submedia than to the subcosta and reaching the wing apex; the wing stump of the forewing slightly larger than that of the hindwing; abdominal papillae absent. Female: the sternite of abdominal segment 7 is about half as long as wide.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Body length 4.5 mm; head oval; antennae 14-segmented, segment 2 longer than segment 4, segment 3 variable in length; labrum entire, oval, not reaching half the length of the mandibles; mandibles strong, incurved, with a spinous apex.
